title: Design System: Η εβδομάδα μου · ΤΗΜΜΥ

display.purpose: Two-line hero headline only; line-mask reveal.

print-event.purpose: Print only: course names in blocks.

print-meta.purpose: Print only: event times, rooms, day meta.

title.purpose: Panel headings: course rail, weekly schedule.

body.purpose: Default text, tabular figures; paragraphs at 1.6 line height.

control.purpose: Buttons, selects, menu items, season switch.

meta.purpose: Course meta, sync time, footer, tooltips.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Ink pills, season thumb, hovered event blocks, tooltips.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, menus, rail drawer, rail button.

shadows.name: highlight
shadows.purpose: Top-edge highlight paired with lifted and floating surfaces.

shadows.name: glass-rim
shadows.purpose: Liquid-glass rim lit from the upper left (plain-CSS approximation; no SVG refraction). Header pill and hero tooltip only, in place of the highlight.

shadows.name: glass-sheen
shadows.purpose: Top sheen layered over the glass fill on the header pill and hero tooltip; same stop as the event blocks' sheen.

shadows.name: glass-fill
shadows.purpose: Header pill fill under the sheen (the hero tooltip keeps 86% surface). Solid surface, no backdrop-filter, under reduced transparency.

shadows.name: sheet-rise
shadows.purpose: Planner sheet top edge over the hero.

shadows.name: header-pill
shadows.purpose: Floating liquid-glass header pill (over var(--glass-sheen),var(--glass-fill) with blur(20px) saturate(1.8)).

motion.name: ease
motion.value: cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Default expo-out for transitions, entrances, drawers, dialogs, and every exit (exit() in app.js, the EASE constant).

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: ~5% overshoot for things that settle into a new value or slot: odometer digits, season thumb, a block shifting to a new slot (520ms). Falls back to the ease curve.

motion.name: there-and-back
motion.value: cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1)
motion.purpose: In-out curve for one-shot pulses that leave rest and return to it: the clash pulse. Never for entrances or exits.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and press transitions on controls; press is scale(.96).

motion.name: odometer
motion.value: .9s spring, 40ms per-digit stagger
motion.purpose: Stat digits roll to new values (countTo).

motion.name: flight
motion.value: 660ms; x cubic-bezier(.55,0,.3,1), y cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.25,1)
motion.purpose: Added course flies on an arc from its rail swatch into each new slot (fly()); the ghost starts at a 3px corner (swatch-like) and opens to 10px in flight, then the block is revealed with the press-in (block-deal) at +600ms, the flight's landing. A ghost whose course is deselected or whose season is left mid-flight is removed. The 3px is a motion detail, not a radius token.

motion.name: season-redeal
motion.value: old blocks: block-leave, 8ms apart, capped at 120ms (not on the phone agenda); new blocks: block-deal from 120ms, min(40, 360/n)ms apart by day (about .5s in all); 3D: old slabs shrink away, new slabs fall in with the squash, 40ms apart (tile-deal)
motion.purpose: Season switch re-deals the week; it replaces the 3D page-turn view transition, now removed. While the 3D week stands in for the blocks it lands in 3D alone. Instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: detail-morph
motion.value: .4s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) view transition (group)
motion.purpose: Course dialog grows out of the clicked block or title (morphOpen()).

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: scale(.96) translateY(-4px) to rest; data menu .2s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), notices .4s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Menus and notices popping in.

motion.name: dialog-exit
motion.value: desktop: opacity 0, translateY(8px) scale(.98), 160ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); phone sheets: translateY(100%), 200ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); backdrop opacity .16s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) (dialog.closing::backdrop)
motion.purpose: closeDialog() via exit(): every close path (buttons, Escape through the cancel event, finished actions) animates out, then closes. Entry stays dialog-in .45s / sheet-up .5s.

motion.name: block-leave
motion.value: 180ms; opacity on the CSS ease keyword cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.25,1) (readable fade; the ease-out would empty it in about two frames), scale(1.04) on var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: A removed block lifts away where it stood (leave()). Desktop grid only; skipped where another block moves into the freed rect and when the week becomes empty. A season switch lifts every old block away this way (season-redeal).

motion.name: clash-pulse
motion.value: outline-offset -2px -> -6px -> -2px, 400ms there-and-back, once; delay = landing (600ms + stagger after a flight, 150ms + stagger after a dealt block)
motion.purpose: Only a block already on the week that has just become conflicting pulses; the newcomer never does. Same season only.

motion.name: toast
motion.value: in: toast-in .4s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) from translate(-50%,-10px) scale(.96); out: same transform with opacity 0, 200ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Update toast eases in from above and leaves upward the way it came.

motion.name: hero-reveal
motion.value: line-in 1.2s ease, .1s/.19s stagger; sub and CTA fade-up at .42s/.54s; sheet-in 1.2s at .36s
motion.purpose: First-viewport entrance.

motion.name: scroll-linked
motion.value: animation-timeline: scroll(root)
motion.purpose: Hero copy lifts away over 60svh, header docks onto a solid bar, rail button rises as the sheet docks.

motion.name: scroll-morph
motion.value: e = smooth((p - .04) / .84); labels out e .35-.65; board/edges dissolve e .55-.95; slab tops to flat fill e .3-.9; planner chrome in e .82-.97 (--chrome); blocks crossfade p .9-1 (--blocks), held at 0 while a deal or throw runs (a dealt block shows on its own via --dealt)
motion.purpose: Above 860px the fixed 3D stage (z 2, pointer-events none, clip-path path evenodd cutting the toolbar/stats band and docked rail) swings the camera straight down and lands the board on the live rect of the planner day columns; slabs flatten (y scale .03) and take the exact flat fill of their blocks (emissive = DOM fill; albedo, clearcoat and env drop). Docked: stage hidden, rendering stops until a 1px .dock-mark just above the docking point (placed by measure(), watched by an IntersectionObserver; hidden in print, removed from the HTML backup) comes into view, a resize, or the drawer closing. Reverses on scroll up. Phones: tilt-away under the sheet. Focus in the week or print forces the 2D week visible.

motion.name: free-view
motion.value: pointerdown catches (aim = current pose); held: yaw/pitch spring to aim (170/19); throw keeps spring velocity soft-limited by m*tanh(v/m) (m 12 yaw, 2.8 pitch; 0 under reduced motion), then drag exp(-dt*3.2) plus constant grip 2.6 rad/s^2 (flick 3 rad/s -> 32deg in .48s, 8 -> 95deg .70s, 16 -> 153deg .82s, 30 -> 177deg .87s); a thrown tilt stays within the same .1 rubber stretch (peak .098), never reaching the elevation clamp; yaw free; pitch [-.4, .86] on a .56 rad base, rubber band past it (STRETCH .1, asymptotic) with spring-back 160/18; camera elevation clamped [.06, pi/2-.04]; zoom eases to aim (120/18); zoom [.8, 1.6] by pinch or Ctrl+wheel; 5px drag threshold; double-click resets
motion.purpose: Hero board free view. Touch: horizontal swipes spin, vertical swipes scroll (.hero touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom). Free view starts only at the top (scroll progress <= 0.002); a drag still held when the page scrolls yields to the homing spring. Orbit springs home once scroll progress > 0 and its offsets scale by (1 - e), so the landing stays exact. A press that travels more than 5px never opens a course.

motion.name: free-view-feel
motion.value: lift .24 while dragging (95/15), one small settle on release (150/13); bank from yaw velocity (clamp .16) and nod from pitch velocity (clamp .12), 110/13; jelly lean rx/rz per slab 170/14 scaled by slab height and distance from centre; squash scale.y from lift velocity (clamp .14); all times calm (1 - e)
motion.purpose: Pseudo-physics weight on the hero board. Reduced motion: drag sets the pose directly, no throw, lift, settle or jelly.

motion.name: drawer-handoff
motion.value: body.rail-open
motion.purpose: Open tablet drawer or phone sheet: 3D stage hidden and not rendered (treated as docked); planner forced fully in (--chrome:1, --blocks:1, empty state opaque) so the fixed layer never draws over the drawer.

motion.name: copy-clearance
motion.value: spring pan; board quad >= 4px right of the copy box (12px above on phones); fades out as e rises
motion.purpose: Keeps headline, sub and CTA in front at any orbit or zoom; the home pose needs no pan.

motion.name: slab-height
motion.value: h = .18 + (min(5, n) - 1) * .22 world units
motion.purpose: Slab height encodes weekly meetings n: once is nearly flat, three or more clearly tall.

motion.name: slab-engraving
motion.value: code up to .24 world units (min .09), pad .09; 300px per unit; walls: box blur radius 2px, slope 9; groove shade 1 - .62 x depth; roughness .55, no clearcoat
motion.purpose: The course code engraved, centred, into each real slab top: a normal-mapped groove in the slab colour that catches the scene light as the board turns; narrow tops shrink the code, then drop the ECE prefix; fades with the board labels over e .35-.65.

motion.name: ring-trace
motion.value: .8s ease infinite alternate, outline-offset -3px to -6px
motion.purpose: Conflict trace pulses its red ring inward inside the block.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp .085
motion.purpose: Page smooth scroll; nested scrollers and dialogs stay native.

motion.name: drawer
motion.value: transform .5s ease
motion.purpose: Rail side drawer and phone bottom sheet; dialogs rise as sheets on phones.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
motion.purpose: Removes all CSS animation and transitions, view transitions, Lenis, fly/morph and the scroll morph; exits (dialogs, toast) are instant, and the block lift-away, the deals and the clash pulse are skipped; the 3D week is a still picture (.hero-stage.still) that scrolls away with the hero.

motion.name: tile-fling
motion.value: grip 600 on ω²·(r+1.5)·(1+0.8h), only while held and spun (drag moved, |ω| > 3), held over it for SLIP .25s; gravity 22; one floor bounce; hop back 420-560ms, 40ms stagger by day (18ms when the page scrolls)
motion.purpose: Spinning the hero board too fast by hand flings slabs onto the studio floor, in a layer that turns with the camera; a flick or a released throw never spills (about 800px/s keeps every slab, about 1400px/s held .25s spills the rim, a full-width hard swipe clears the board); once the spin calms they hop back to their slots, Monday to Friday, landing with a squash. Not under reduced motion.

motion.name: tile-throw
motion.value: fires once p < .9, once per planner visit; up to the top edge in ~0.3s; fall 300ms each, 40ms stagger by day (10ms heading back down)
motion.purpose: Leaving the docked planner upward throws the slabs off the top of the screen once per visit, only once the scroll is below 90% so overshooting the planner's top never throws the week; they fall back onto the board when the scroll rests 160ms, the board nears the hero (p < .25) or the page heads back down. Desktop and tablet only; not under reduced motion.

motion.name: tile-deal
motion.value: DEAL 40ms per tile, by day then start time; landing: gravity 22 from above, squash .22 (spring 260/16), no overshoot; intro from 520ms, at most 16 steps; scroll down: lift once p > .05 (intro tiles come along: falling ones lifted where they are, unshown ones keep their moment and arrive from above into the hover), 12ms apart, hover .55 units (spring 240, damping exp(-28·dt)), dealt at e >= .995 (or scroll rest 200ms, scroll up, back at the top), gap min(40, 360/n)ms (about .5s in all), fall 200ms on u·(.35+.65u), then hand-over: tile hides, block --dealt: 1, scale(1.06) -> none from its centre, box-shadow var(--shadow-md) -> rest, 180ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: One landing for the 3D tiles: the intro, rebuilds, the hop back after a spin and the fall from the sky all land this way. The first committed scroll down from the top (a jiggle never does) lifts the tiles, taking any still in the intro along, and deals them onto the landed planner, each handing over to its own block; the canvas stays on, other blocks stay hidden and the stage does not dock until the deal ends; handed-over tiles come back if the board leaves the landed pose. Desktop and tablet only; not under reduced motion.

motion.name: block-deal
motion.value: opacity 0 -> 1, scale(1.06) -> none from the centre (transform-origin center; blocks keep a top origin for the hover lift), box-shadow var(--shadow-md) -> rest, 220ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), fill backwards (stampIn()); DEAL 40ms stagger, at most 12 steps
motion.purpose: One landing for the 2D week's blocks, the echo of the 3D deal: new blocks arrive a touch larger and press down to size, Monday to Friday. A course flying in from the list is revealed this way at the flight's landing. Skipped, like every 2D block animation (lift-away, flight, clash pulse), while the 3D week stands in for the blocks (--blocks below 1, no focus in #calendarWrap): one landing per change. Not under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: vertical day agenda, rail as bottom sheet with scrim, dialogs as bottom sheets, 24px sheet radius, 3D tilt-away instead of the scroll morph.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Full-width week, rail as side drawer.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: min-width: docked 340px rail beside the week.

breakpoints.name: lane-time-name
breakpoints.purpose: Narrow lane: start time plus the compact name, soft-hyphenated at Greek syllables (app.js hyphenate).

breakpoints.name: lane-time-code
breakpoints.value: 80px (container, screen); also lessons of an hour or less below 112px
breakpoints.purpose: Narrower lane: start time plus course code.

breakpoints.name: lane-number
breakpoints.purpose: Four or more parallel lessons: the shared ECE prefix hides, the course number stays.

narrative.overview:
The student's own timetable is a product shot. It sits as glossy 3D slabs on a floating board in a neutral photo studio, lit like an object on a seamless backdrop, and the planner sheet rises over it like a page slid onto the set. Everything around the object stays quiet: studio greys, ink type, one neon accent. The colour lives in the courses themselves.

Below the fold the studio becomes a calm, editorial work surface. The week is the canvas and is never cropped sideways. Pills for everything you press, soft 20-28px surfaces, 12px event blocks, giant grotesk numerals for the stats. The signature move is a scroll morph: on desktop and tablet the 3D board swings to a top-down view and lands exactly on the planner's week, and the slabs become its flat blocks. The tiles are objects and the board is their tray: whenever the week changes place or content, the tiles leave the tray and are dealt back Monday to Friday (by day, then start time), 40ms apart and the whole deal held to about half a second, with one landing. In 3D a tile falls, accelerating under gravity, and squashes as it lands; on the 2D week a block arrives a touch larger and presses down to size. The intro, the hop back after a spin, the fall back from the sky, the scroll down onto the planner, new blocks and the season switch all deal this way. Elsewhere motion is physical and springy: digits roll, the season thumb and blocks moving to a new slot settle with a small overshoot, and a course flies on an arc into its slot. Exits are shorter than entrances and leave the way things came, on the ease-out: dialogs drop and fade, phone sheets slide back down, a removed block lifts away where it stood, the update toast lifts away. The one exception: a removed block's opacity runs on the CSS `ease` keyword so the fade stays readable, while its scale stays on the ease-out. A block that has just started to clash pulses its red ring once on the there-and-back curve. Every one of these collapses to an instant, static path under reduced motion.

The world is modelled on butter.video, chosen by the user. Rejected and not to return: the cool-grey, electric-blue, pastel-course "premium product app" world set in Commissioner with 16/10 radii.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral studio greys with an off-white (light) or ink (dark) planner sheet; no tinted neutrals.
Ink is the primary action colour; hot pink is a single neon note, never a fill for large surfaces.
Nine vivid course hues, full-strength on event blocks, with ink or white text chosen by contrast.
Geologica everywhere, tabular figures by default, display sizes with tight negative tracking.
Pill controls, soft rectangles for surfaces, 12px for event blocks.
Soft layered shadows in light mode; hairlines take over in dark mode.
The hero's 3D week and the planner's 2D week are one object: scrolling morphs one into the other.
One landing: tiles and blocks are dealt Monday to Friday, 40ms apart, the whole deal held to about half a second; a 3D tile falls under gravity and squashes, a 2D block presses from 1.06 to size.

Three curves: the spring (~5% overshoot) for things that settle into a new value or slot, the ease-out for transitions, presses and exits, the there-and-back in-out for one-shot pulses; everything static under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Neon Rule
rules.body: Hot pink is the only accent and it appears as small marks (a full stop, a day pill, a count, a hover), never as a button fill or a section background. Primary actions are ink.

rules.name: The Colour Is the Course Rule
rules.body: Saturation belongs to the course palette. Chrome stays grey and ink; no course is ever grey, and no course hue is pure green, amber or red, so courses can never be mistaken for a state. One exception, accepted by the user: the liquid glass on the header pill and the hero tooltip saturates what lies beneath it (1.8), so a course passing under the frost reads as slightly richer colour, never as chrome colour. Over a cobalt slab the tooltip shows a faint blue with legible text; a coloured slab under the header pill is untested.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every semantic state carries a second signal: passed is a filled green swatch plus a check icon; review is a dashed amber outline plus a hatch; overlap is a solid red outline plus a warning icon.

rules.name: The Numbers Are the Headline Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular everywhere, and the week's totals are set at display scale, not tucked into small chips.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geologica carries every role; hierarchy comes from size, weight and tracking, never from a second display face.

rules.name: The No Sideways Week Rule
rules.body: The week never scrolls horizontally. The grid is a 54px hour axis plus five equal day columns, whatever they hold. Parallel lessons split their day into lanes, and narrow lanes step down by container width. At 112px or less a lane shows its start time and the name, set compact with soft hyphens at Greek syllable breaks. At 80px or less, and for lessons of an hour or less, it shows start time plus course code. At 60px or less it shows the code only. At 50px or less the shared ECE prefix drops and only the course number remains. The full name always stays in the tooltip and dialog. Margin notes move beside the week only when the busiest day still gets 150px per lane.

rules.name: The Print Is Its Own Layout Rule
rules.body: Print is one A4 landscape sheet in the selected theme: chrome hidden, the sheet and blocks exactly as on screen (light or dark), no today marking, the week scaled to fit and forced fully visible, the print type ramp, all motion and shadows off. Nothing on the printed page sizes itself with viewport units, because Chrome's print preview resolves them against the browser window and a window-tall page spills a blank second sheet.

rules.name: The Press, Don't Lift Rule
rules.body: Controls press (scale 0.96 on active) and never rise on hover. Only event blocks lift (2px) on hover, because they are objects on the board, and only where a fine pointer can hover ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)), so a tap never leaves a block stuck raised.

rules.name: The Rings Inside Rule
rules.body: State and highlight outlines on event blocks sit inside the block (negative offset), never outside it.

rules.name: The Hairline in the Dark Rule
rules.body: In dark mode every raised surface (dialog, menu, tooltip, drawer, sheet) gets a 1px hairline edge, since shadows cannot read on ink.

dos: **Do** make primary actions ink pills; keep hot pink to small marks (full stop, today, counts, hover).
**Do** give every pressable thing a full pill shape and the 0.96 press.
**Do** let free-view interactions (orbit, zoom) yield to scroll and to the copy: plain wheel scrolls, the board springs home on scroll, and it never covers the headline.
**Do** pick block text colour by contrast (ink or white) for any course hue, including user-chosen ones.
**Do** pair every success, warning and danger state with an icon, dashes or an outline.

**Do** use the spring easing (`linear()` with ~5% overshoot, fallback cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) for things that settle into a new value or slot (digits, the season thumb, a block shifting lanes), the ease-out (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) for the 2D press-in and for exits, and the there-and-back curve (cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1)) only for one-shot pulses that return to rest; make every animation, view transition, smooth scroll and 3D loop disappear under reduced motion.

**Do** deal tiles and blocks onto the week Monday to Friday (by day, then start time), 40ms apart and the whole deal held to about half a second (bigger weeks close the gap), with one landing per change: in 3D a fall that accelerates under gravity and ends in a squash, never a spring that overshoots into the board; in 2D a press from scale 1.06 to size about the block's centre, with a fade and the lifted shadow coming down to rest (220ms on the ease-out). While the 3D week stands in for the planner's blocks, the change lands in 3D alone.

**Do** make exits shorter than their entrances (160-200ms) and send things out the way they came in, on the ease-out; the one exception is a removed block, whose opacity runs on the CSS `ease` keyword so the fade stays readable while its scale stays on the ease-out. For the opposite direction use mirrored keyframes, never `animation-direction: reverse`, which turns the ease-out into an ease-in.
**Do** keep five equal day columns and step narrow lanes down (time and name, time and code, code, number) rather than widening a busy day.
**Do** keep the week fully visible without horizontal scroll at every width, and keep print as a dedicated A4 landscape layout.
**Do** keep the 3D week and the planner's week the same object: same course colours, the same five equal columns and lanes, one hand-over sequence with never two hour axes on screen.
**Do** use tabular figures and display-scale numerals for the week's totals.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour or fill buttons, panels or headers with neon pink.
**Don't** use grey, pure green, amber or red as a course colour.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or uppercase tracked labels; Geologica in sentence case carries every role.
**Don't** use square or small-radius buttons; nothing pressable sits between pill and rectangle.
**Don't** lift controls on hover or use hard offset shadows; controls press, only event blocks lift.
**Don't** draw state or highlight rings outside an event block.
**Don't** tint the neutrals cool or warm; the studio greys are neutral.
